title: Psalms Wax Lamp
subject: Torts
stem:
Lydia runs a paid private Psalms calligraphy workshop in her garage studio. During the class, Ruth reached across the worktable for a sheet of parchment and brushed her forearm against an exposed brass warming lamp used to soften sealing wax. Ruth was burned. The next morning, Lydia installed a small wire guard around the lamp. Lydia admits that the guard could have been installed before Ruth was burned, but she denies that reasonable care required a guard under the conditions that existed during the class.

For breach, what is the best use of the later installation?
call: For breach, what is the best use of the later installation?

choices.A: It may matter only to feasibility if feasibility is genuinely disputed, but it does not replace the breach analysis.
choices.B: It proves Ruth was contributorily negligent because Lydia added the guard after the burn.
choices.C: It conclusively proves Lydia breached her duty before Ruth was burned.
choices.D: It is always irrelevant to every issue because it happened after the injury.

rightExplanation: A is correct. The later wire guard does not answer the breach question by itself. The breach question still asks whether reasonable care required the guard before Ruth was burned. Gold Key: a later safety change is not proof that the earlier condition was negligent; its limited use is a non-breach purpose such as feasibility, and only if that purpose is genuinely disputed. Silver Key: lock the call to “best use for breach.” Do not let the later fix become a shortcut for deciding whether the earlier setup was unreasonable.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: “Conclusive proof” is an overclaim. A later guard may feel like an admission, but conclusive skips the breach analysis.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: “Always irrelevant to every issue” is an overclaim. The answer denies all limited uses.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: Ruth’s contributory negligence is the wrong target. The call asks breach by Lydia.

c3.label: RESIDUAL A
c3.text: The only answer that keeps the use narrow and keeps breach analysis separate.

c3.label: CALL / anchor check
c3.text: Gold Key confirms the residual: later safety changes are not breach proof; feasibility is a limited use only if genuinely disputed.

studentScript: The later guard cannot replace breach. If feasibility were disputed, it might matter there. Here feasibility is admitted. A.

A.signal: Narrow conditional answer; it refuses to treat the later guard as breach proof.
A.lawyer: Fed. R. Evid. 407 permits later remedial-measure evidence for feasibility if disputed and bars it to prove negligence; breach remains reasonable care under prior circumstances.

B.signal: The call asks whether Lydia breached; this answer talks about Ruth's contributory negligence.
B.lawyer: A defendant's later installation does not establish the plaintiff's lack of care.

C.signal: The word conclusively skips the breach analysis.
C.lawyer: Later remedial measures are not admissible to prove negligence or culpable conduct and are not an admission of prior breach.

D.signal: Always irrelevant to every issue says too much.
D.lawyer: Later remedial measures can be admitted for a limited non-prohibited purpose, including feasibility if disputed.

goldKeys.statement: A later safety fix is not proof that the earlier condition was negligent. Its limited use is a non-breach purpose such as feasibility, and only if that purpose is genuinely disputed.
goldKeys.trigger: Defendant changes the condition after the injury.
goldKeys.authority: Fed. R. Evid. 407; Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical and Emotional Harm §3.

silverKeys.statement: Lock the call to use, not hindsight. First cut the two extremes: later fix proves everything, later fix proves nothing.
silverKeys.trigger: A post-injury safety change appears in a breach question.

remediation.title: Later Fix Is Not Hindsight Liability
remediation.signal: Post-injury repair, added guard, new warning, new traction, or changed procedure.
remediation.studentMove: Separate prior breach from later feasibility.
remediation.tinyRule: Later fix is not breach proof; feasibility only if genuinely disputed.
remediation.trap: They fixed it later, so they must have breached earlier.
